reason: A volcano in the ocean seems like a useful way to establish an island habitat for the birds.
expectation: I expect an island to form, though its role in the food web is not yet clear.

alternatives.reason: Birds crossing mountains could advance migration, but I want to establish the island first.

effect: The volcanic island provides a potential habitat; next I can work on the birds' journey.
reaction: The seafloor mountain building above the ocean was a satisfying explanation.
reason: This is the only available combination, and crossing mountains fits the migration goal.
expectation: I expect birds to cross the mountains, perhaps establishing a migration route.

effect: The birds can now cross mountain barriers; seasonal changes may connect their journeys to migration.
reaction: The connection between flight and distant feeding grounds makes sense.
reason: This is the only offered combination and directly suggests seasonal migration.
expectation: I expect the birds to migrate between feeding or breeding grounds as seasons change.

effect: Seasonal journeys establish migration between feeding and breeding grounds; the island can now be connected to those journeys.
reaction: The link between changing food supplies and migration is clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may connect migrating birds to the island.
expectation: I expect the birds to reach or settle on the volcanic island, though their exact role there is uncertain.

effect: Birds have established a population separated from the mainland, setting up the possibility of differences developing over generations.
reaction: The transition from migration to an isolated breeding population makes sense.
reason: This is the only offered combination and may develop variation in the island population.
expectation: I expect inherited differences to emerge in the island birds, perhaps affecting their songs over generations.

effect: The island population now has distinct songs, shaped by both inherited variation and learned traditions; the remaining combination connects it to food webs.
reaction: The distinction between inherited variation and learned song was interesting.
reason: This is the only offered combination and directly addresses the food-web goal.
expectation: I expect the food web to support the island birds and migrating flocks, though the exact connection is uncertain.

effect: The final combination connected the distinct bird populations to broader food webs and completed the chapter's goal.
reaction: The community-wide perspective was a satisfying conclusion, though the connection to migrating flocks remained broad.

mostWorthwhile.text: Developing different island songs was most worthwhile: it distinguished inherited variation from learned song traditions.

leastWorthwhile.text: Crossing the mountains was a clear but fairly predictable prerequisite, especially as it was the only offered combination.

surprise.text: I was interested that learned traditions as well as inherited variation could contribute to differences in bird song.

arbitrary.text: Combining different songs directly with a food web felt somewhat abstract; the result linked birds to communities, but the songs themselves did not clearly explain that connection.

continue.text: Yes, I would continue for more connections like the distinction between inherited variation and learned behavior, though the mostly single-option sequence offered limited decisions.
